FYI: there won't be a "superstar of the sport" because basketball is unique in how one superstar can dominate every game. Hockey places a much greater emphasis on depth, but I think that's just about every team sport compared to basketball. Your categories or scoring system will influence who's valuable and who isn't. Can't really give you more specific advice without knowing what those are. Beyond the first handful of superstars, whether you're in a category or points league will change who you should target.  But generally speaking, centers put up some of the best numbers, but the league will always have lots of quality centers available. Your first pick in a draft might very well be a center. The top wingers will go quickly as well, because they'll still put up huge point totals, but the position isn't as deep as center. Defensemen that score a lot are scarce and you'll want to prioritize snagging at least one of them in your first three or four picks (this is an important way you can get a leg up on non-hockey fan leaguemates). Getting an elite goalie early in the draft can help, but some league settings place less emphasis on goalies. One team has been the subject of much debate this year. They've been a doormat for a long time and then they've come out of nowhere under a new coach (who many had written off as a coach, and for good reason). A breakout rookie defenseman and a top goalie have been standout performers so far this year, you'll want to look into those guys. Which leads me to another important point for noobs....don't overload too many guys from one team. The league tends to clump most of its games on Tuesdays, Thursdays, and Saturdays. If you have five guys from the same club, you'll run into problems where you can't play everybody on the same night (so their production is wasted) and the other four nights you've got nobody playing. The rule of thumb is don't take more than two guys from the same team.

Great read, as always. He's done it again. Definitely getting a quasi-Pearl Harbor vibe to this, where the attack is a tactical success but strategically inconclusive. The enemy's still in the fight, at least for the moment. The opposing force is going to lash out. Whether they have sufficient remaining infrastructure to continue supporting large-scale operations in the long term, I don't know. Individual raiding parties might do fine with Napoleon-style fighting (in other words, living off the land as they go), but I don't see how they could maintain the whole Swarm-of-Swarms in one place for long that way. Speaking of the S-o-S itself, I'm curious about their capability to emergency-scramble the entire force from a standing start. They have a finite amount of time (three hours?) to get a massive number of bodies to battle stations and launched. It'd be kind of like an aircraft carrier trying to scramble its entire complement of ~100 planes while the ship is sinking or something. There'd be a massive traffic jam at whatever internal chokepoints exist. And at some point, the infrastructure damage will start interfering with continuing to launch ships (power outage? fire? king-shit EM pulse? decompression taking critical machinery offline?). I wouldn't expect the opposing force to be real diligent about about something like keeping up-to-date contingency plans and procedures for abandoning the Hive. On top of all *that*, then there's whatever confusion accompanies the palace coup. I guess the telepathy thing helps with command & control, but still. What if there's even a brief schism between the two factions? Let alone the outbreak of a full-scale civil war while the Hive and its military infrastructure is literally falling out of the sky. And then there's whatever impact these events will have on the opposing force's reserves of, uh, livestock. An army marches on its stomach, and all that. So the Swarm is probably going to be diminished at least somewhat, the only question is how much. That makes me wonder if the leader is capable of attempting to come to the negotiating table and lead the post-coup faction into something like a truce with galactic society, because they're losing a mind-boggling amount of resources, no matter what else happens. Unless they've got more of these Hives somewhere else, I suppose.... TL,DR: Can't wait til the next chapter :D
